classification.summary: AnyswapV4Router: anySwapOutUnderlyingWithPermit did not validate the token, letting attackers pull WETH from accounts with stale approvals (WETH has no permit; fallback executed).

loss.notes: Migrated from legacy lossUsd/lossOther. The legacy corpus did not consistently distinguish gross from net loss or record valuation provenance.

limitations: Target identity and code history came from the v1 snapshot row originally at protocols/multichain.json; no semantic revalidation was inherited.
The executing code artifact and its code hash have not been established in structured evidence.

sources.note: onchain review (no exploit tx: incident block located by binary-searching eth_getBlockByNumber to measurement.incidentTimestamp -> ethereum block 14029360, 2022-01-18T12:00:00Z). AnyswapV4Router 0x6b7a87899490EcE95443e979cA9485CBE7E71522 was created at block 12657964, 2021-06-18T10:44:06Z. It is not a proxy: zero DELEGATECALL opcodes in the runtime, no EIP-1967 Upgraded event, and byte-identical eth_getCode at the creation block and the incident block, so the deployment basis is exact. Storage was checked against the verified named layout (cast storage): slot 0 `_oldMPC`, slot 1 `_newMPC`, slot 2 `_newMPCEffectiveTime`; the only pre-incident storage change (slot 0 at block 12806663, 2021-07-11T14:56:16Z -> 0x8b44a687224496276811555efa3f2d0acd667a72) is an MPC key rotation, not a code change.

exploit tx backfilled and verified onchain (block 14037237; AnyswapV4Router victim in receipt logs): the canonical DeFiHackLabs-referenced attack tx of the Jan 2022 permit flaw - many copycat txs followed public disclosure

limitations: Classification and loss came from the v1 snapshot row originally at protocols/multichain.json; legacy measurement.status=OK is provenance only.
The legacy USD loss lacks uniformly structured valuation provenance.
